newsitem.title: UK: Strike called off at RTZ's Kennecott.
newsitem.headline: Strike called off at RTZ's Kennecott.

text.p: RTZ Corp Plc said the union at its Kennecott Utah Copper Corp unit in Utah has called off a strike by some 1,800 workers which began on Wednesday.

A spokesman for RTZ in London said following a meeting between union officials and the company, the union had advised that the workforce would be returning to work at 1500 local time on Friday. The Kennecott smelter had been operating at a reduced level.
The spokesman said negotiations would now continue on a new contract at Kennecott, which operates a 310,000 short tons per year smelter. The previous three-year contract expired on September 30.
The strike had also affected Kennecott's mines, concentrators, power plant and refinery.

Three months copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) fell to a quote of $1,928/1,930 per tonne on the news of the strike settlement, a drop of around $8, but almost immediately began rising again when the LME announced a big fall of 19,125 tonnes in copper stocks.
At 0810 GMT copper was quoted at $1,938/1,943.
